Here are two primary reasons a bridge might use a suspension design:

1.  **To Span Long Distances**: Suspension bridges are the most efficient design for crossing very wide bodies of water or deep valleys. Unlike beam or arch bridges, which rely on intermediate supports (piers) that are difficult or impossible to build in deep water or unstable ground, suspension bridges can span several miles using only two main towers and anchorages on either side.
